Mais ces hommes et ces femmes étaient-ils vraiment ces barbares décrits par les chroniqueurs du Moyen Age ? Les conquêtes de territoires nourrissaient-elles leur quotidien ?

programme.title: Le dessous des cartes : l'essentiel

programme.title: Nazi Megastructures

Ces structures étant très visibles et imposantes, elles ont été conçues pour résister aux tirs et aux bombes ennemies. Des abris subsistent encore aujourd'hui et sont l'exemple de l'imagination sans limite de l'époque. Ces forteresses sous-marines voulues par Hitler, font parties des constructions les plus incroyables de la Seconde Guerre mondiale.

programme.title: French Connection
programme.desc: The founders of Marseille’s drug empire were Corsican-Marseille underworld bosses and Italian-American mobsters who joined forces in the heroin market after the Second World War. Raw material from Turkey was smuggled to Marseille, where chemists who learned their formulas within their families processed it in secret laboratories. The exceptionally pure drug was then transported by every possible means to New York for distribution. This expanding network soon became one of the largest criminal organisations of all time, known as the French Connection. The source describes thousands of tonnes leaving French laboratories for the American market rather than France.

programme.title: Israël : Comment sauver la démocratie

programme.desc: Le 2 août 1990, l'Iraq envahissait le Koweït. Quatre heures plus tard, le vol BA 149 reliant Londres Heathrow à Kuala Lumpur, avec 400 personnes à bord, a atterri au Koweït pour une escale prévue. Lorsque Hussein a annoncé au monde entier que les passagers et l'équipage étaient désormais ses otages, une crise internationale qui a rapidement dégénéré et duré quatre mois a éclaté. Les passagers et l'équipage, qui n'étaient pas au courant, sont devenus les pions d'un jeu impitoyable mené par le dictateur. Pendant trente ans, les autorités britanniques ont nié ce qui s'était passé à bord de ce vol. La vérité n'est révélée qu'aujourd'hui.

During the Second World War, Atkins was responsible for 470 secret agents in Britain’s Special Operations Executive. Her section included nearly 40 women spies sent behind enemy lines. Determined to trace those who vanished on their missions, Vera kept all their files at home, defying the authorities.

Napoléon III doit désormais légitimer son trône auprès des anciennes dynasties qui contrôlent l'Europe et redonner à la France la place qu'elle a perdue. programme.desc: En avril 1867, Charles Bonnin, qui a mené sa carrière avec brio, occupe désormais la place de rédacteur en chef du journal. Alors qu'en apparence l'empire français semble plus fort que jamais, il est en réalité secoué par une profonde crise politique. Napoléon III a, depuis 1860, décidé de libéraliser les institutions du pays et se retrouve isolé comme jamais auparavant. Sa base politique traditionnelle et conservatrice lui reproche ses velléités libérales alors que l'opposition s'insurge de la lenteur de l'Empereur à rendre ses libertés au peuple. Pour ne rien arranger, Napoléon III est gravement malade. Les troubles politiques intérieurs ne sont pas les seuls dangers qui menacent l'Empire. A Nuremberg, détruite par les bombes, 21 hauts dignitaires nazis se retrouvent sur le banc des accusés d'un procès historique, qui doit asseoir la nécessité d'une justice internationale. Cette approche, portée par le procureur américain Robert Jackson, s'impose contre les tenants d'une justice expéditive, Churchill et Staline en tête. Près de 300 figures de la presse et de la littérature viennent y assister, logées au château de Faber-Castell. Joseph Kessel côtoie John Dos Passos, Madeleine Jacob, Boris Polevoï et de nombreux correspondants de guerre chinois, brésiliens, australiens. Mais le procès s'enlise, plombé par la lourdeur de la procédure. C'est alors que le procureur Jackson chamboule tout, en diffusant une archive témoignant de l'horreur des camps de concentration.

programme.title: Notre Histoire de France
programme.desc: A la fin du VIIIe siècle, le nouveau roi Charlemagne rêve de créer un empire aussi puissant que celui des Romains. Il part à la conquête de l'Europe. Il est finalement couronné empereur à Rome par le pape Léon III le 24 ou 25 décembre 800, un titre et un pouvoir disparus en Occident depuis 476. L'historienne Geneviève Bührer-Thierry, spécialiste du pouvoir royal au haut Moyen Age s'est particulièrement penchée sur cette figure mythique. Elle fait le point sur les connaissances relatives à ce personnage qui a cristallisé bien des fantasmes. Des scènes fictionnalisées, commentées par le comédien Tomer Sisley, rend accessible le travail des chercheurs.

programme.title: Méduses : Les souveraines des océans

programme.title: L'album SS retrouvé
programme.desc: En 2016, un album contenant 250 photos inédites d'officiels nazis est découvert aux USA par Stephan Hördler, éminent historien spécialiste de l'Holocauste, qui comprend immédiatement la valeur inestimable de cet album. L'album réunit les photographies d'une "bande d'amis", tous issus de la même région d'Allemagne, tous devenus SS. De 1928 à 1943, l'album photo permet ainsi de suivre leur parcours. Hördler a mené l'enquête, rapprochant les photos de l'album à d'autres plus connues, les visages de ces hommes avec ceux de cadres de camps de concentration pour finir par révéler que c'est à Lichtencburg que ces jeunes hommes ont été formés, une "école" pour futurs bourreaux des camps et les liens de camaraderie et le réseau informel qui leur permettront de s'entraider, même la guerre terminée.

programme.desc: On 6 June 1944, as the landings began on Normandy’s beaches, Hitler realised he needed reinforcements and called on the Das Reich SS armoured division, an elite unit based in Montauban. Fifteen thousand men set out with two missions: reach Normandy as quickly as possible and clear the French resistance groups likely to stand in their way. Made up of young recruits, including Alsatians, and veterans versed in punitive methods, the unit committed repeated atrocities, notably at Tulle and, still more horrifically, in the massacre of Oradour-sur-Glane’s population in Limousin.

Mais pour les forces alliés, d'immenses défis restent pourtant à relever : il leur faut reconstruire un continent entièrement dévasté, mais aussi panser les plaies des populations civiles, affaiblies par la faim et animées par une soif de vengeance. Plus de 40 millions de personnes déplacées par la guerre rêvent de retrouver leurs foyers et, bien que les armes aient été déposées, la violence continue de régner. Après la peste brune, il semble qu'un nouveau conflit menace.

programme.desc: À la fin des années 1970, en pleine guerre froide, la tension entre l'Est et l'Ouest est d'autant plus tangible que l'Europe occidentale se trouve à portée de tirs des ogives nucléaires soviétiques. En décembre 1979, l'Otan décide d'un programme de déploiement sur le Vieux Continent de plus de 500 missiles américains. Cette surenchère aux armes nucléaires plonge une partie de la population dans l'angoisse d'une guerre atomique. Au Royaume-Uni, des femmes se regroupent pour partager leur peur du futur et décident d'agir. Le 27 août 1981, une marche à travers le pays de Galles est organisée jusqu'à la base militaire de Greenham, en Angleterre.

L'Histoire porte un regard différent sur ces événements.

programme.title: Momentos impactantes de la Historia
programme.desc: Un piloto logra saltar del avión en el último instante, justo antes de que la aeronave se estrelle contra unas rocas. El angustioso momento en el que un motorista intenta escapar de un bosque lleno de árboles que se caen. Un espeleólogo debe recurrir a su pericia para escapar cuando queda atrapado entre la espada y la pared. El Hindenburg, orgullo de la Alemania nazi, explota y arde por los cuatro costados mientras sobrevuela Nueva Jersey en 1937, desatando el misterio. Tony Harris y su equipo de expertos examinan las pistas y averiguan la verdad de los hechos y por qué ocurrieron.

programme.title: Un día en la Historia de España: 20 de octubre de 1982
programme.desc: El 20 de octubre de 1982, Valencia vivió una de las mayores catástrofes hidrológicas de su historia reciente. Tras varios días de lluvias torrenciales, la presa de Tous cedió y una enorme riada inundó numerosas localidades de la Ribera del Júcar. Miles de personas tuvieron que abandonar sus hogares y los daños fueron devastadores. La conocida como Pantanada de Tous marcó un antes y un después en la gestión de las inundaciones en España y quedó grabada en la memoria colectiva de varias generaciones. Más de cuarenta años después, la DANA que golpeó la provincia de Valencia en 2024 volvió a poner de manifiesto la vulnerabilidad del territorio ante los fenómenos extremos y la necesidad de seguir mejorando la prevención y la respuesta frente a las inundaciones.

programme.title: File, los últimos templos del antiguo Egipto
programme.desc: Los templos de File fueron el último baluarte de la antigua religión egipcia y son una de las atracciones más emblemáticas de la época ptolemaica. Originalmente se hallaban situados en la isla del mismo nombre, que ahora está bajo el agua. Al igual que Abu Simbel, File fue objeto de una inusual operación de rescate arqueológico: en la década de 1970, los mejores científicos, arquitectos y egiptólogos del mundo se embarcaron en la titánica tarea de desmantelar, pieza por pieza, las 50.000 toneladas de piedra que componían los templos y reconstruirlos, exactamente igual que antes, en la isla vecina de Agilkia. Este especial revela los increíbles retos tecnológicos superados en el pasado para construir File, y de nuevo en el siglo XX para reubicarlo y protegerlo de las aguas.

programme.title: Nefertiti: en busca de la tumba perdida
programme.desc: ¿Dónde se encuentra la tumba de la famosa reina del antiguo Egipto? Nos sumergiremos en el corazón de la ciencia y a través del tiempo para penetrar en el misterio de la tumba perdida de Nefertiti.

programme.title: El círculo de poder del Tercer Reich
programme.desc: Tras el final de la Segunda Guerra Mundial, surgieron numerosas leyendas en torno a la vida de Adolf Hitler. Sus colaboradores supervivientes intentaron presentarlo como único responsable de la guerra y del genocidio, alimentando teorías sobre una supuesta patología o incapacidad emocional. Sin embargo, el dictador mantuvo estrechos vínculos personales. Este episodio analiza sus relaciones con una sucesión de mujeres más jóvenes.

programme.title: El círculo de poder del Tercer Reich
programme.desc: Durante décadas se afirmó que Adolf Hitler carecía de vida privada. No obstante, en su residencia del Obersalzberg estaba rodeado de un entorno íntimo casi familiar. Eva Braun organizaba la vida cotidiana y actuaba como su secretaria privada. Quienes accedían a este círculo debían mostrar lealtad absoluta, mientras familias como las de Goebbels y Bormann eran conscientes de los crímenes que se fraguaban en aquel idílico entorno alpino.

programme.title: El círculo de poder del Tercer Reich
programme.desc: Tras la invasión de Polonia, poco cambia inicialmente en la vida privada de la élite nazi. Hitler se retira con frecuencia a su círculo íntimo en el Obersalzberg, mientras miles de judíos europeos son deportados a campos de exterminio como Buchenwald. Allí reinan el terror y la muerte, a escasa distancia de la vida acomodada que llevan el comandante del campo, Karl Otto Koch, y su esposa Ilse junto a sus hijos.

programme.title: El círculo de poder del Tercer Reich
programme.desc: La salud de Hitler se deteriora y se somete a los cuestionables tratamientos de su médico personal, quien le administra cócteles de drogas. Hermann Göring pierde influencia, afectado por su adicción a la morfina, mientras Joseph Goebbels asume un papel central organizando la 'guerra total'. Cuando la derrota es inevitable, Hitler y su entorno se refugian en el búnker de Berlín, donde se consuma su final.

programme.title: The Rise and Fall of Civilisations

programme.title: Un día en la Historia de España: 20 de octubre de 1982
programme.desc: El 20 de octubre de 1982, Valencia vivió una de las mayores catástrofes hidrológicas de su historia reciente. Tras varios días de lluvias torrenciales, la presa de Tous cedió y una enorme riada inundó numerosas localidades de la Ribera del Júcar. Miles de personas tuvieron que abandonar sus hogares y los daños fueron devastadores. La conocida como Pantanada de Tous marcó un antes y un después en la gestión de las inundaciones en España y quedó grabada en la memoria colectiva de varias generaciones. Más de cuarenta años después, la DANA que golpeó la provincia de Valencia en 2024 volvió a poner de manifiesto la vulnerabilidad del territorio ante los fenómenos extremos y la necesidad de seguir mejorando la prevención y la respuesta frente a las inundaciones.

programme.title: Misterios revelados con Danny Trejo
programme.desc: Algunos hallazgos accidentales pueden ser letales: secretos mortales, armas olvidadas y maldiciones legendarias revelan los hallazgos más letales bajo tierra, agua y hasta en el espacio.

programme.title: Misterios revelados con Danny Trejo

programme.title: Misterios revelados con Danny Trejo

programme.title: Grandes guerreros de la historia
programme.desc: El espartano fue uno de los soldados más temidos y eficaces del mundo entre los siglos VII y IV a. C. Su disciplina y dedicación a la preparación militar comenzaban desde la infancia. Equipado con lanza, escudo y armadura, derrotaba a sus enemigos mediante tácticas precisas y gran valentía, convirtiéndose en el pilar de la falange espartana.

programme.title: Grandes guerreros de la historia
programme.desc: Su dominio del tiro con arco a caballo y su gran movilidad convirtieron al mongol en uno de los guerreros más eficaces de su época. Bajo el liderazgo de Gengis Kan, en el siglo XIII, los mongoles emplearon tácticas avanzadas y una férrea disciplina para conquistar amplias regiones de Asia, Europa y Oriente Próximo. Su capacidad de adaptación, organización y ataque los convirtió en una fuerza dominante y temida desde China hasta Europa occidental.

programme.title: Nature's Force
programme.desc: Snow is a fascinating world of crystals that animals, plants, and humans have had to adapt to, in order to benefit from its best and survive its worst attributes. Some communities live with Tornadoes by building homes with survival features and rather than get out of their paths, they rely on warning systems and classifications. And behind all great weather events is Wind, find out how and why it can change from a gentle breeze into a devastating gale force and where does it go? Nature's... force can be mystical and puzzling and the Sunshower has been the subject of myths and legends and supe rstitions, but it does have a scientific explanation.

programme.title: Nature's Force
programme.desc: What is La Nina and how is it being monitored? Find out the effects and the reach that this system is influencing. How did Indian Summer get its name and what is the science behind the phenomenon? Winter is the season that has the biggest effect on the planet, animal behaviour and often brings out the worst that nature can bring. Nature's Halo is a magical sight with a scientific explanation. The story of and lessons from Hurricane Katrina give us a great understanding of the ferocity and... speed that nature can unleash.

programme.title: Show Me Where You Live
programme.desc: Show me where you live is a documentary series that aims to answer the following question: How can human beings claim ownership to a space so that they can live safely within it, function as a society, and above all be in harmony with the environment around them? As we discover cultures and emblematic populations, we follow Philippe Simay who is at the heart of Inhabiting the World and represents its identity and originality. Philippe takes us on an epic adventure around the Human Habitat... and sets the tone for the journey. As a humanist and philosopher, Philippe is a tireless surveyor of t he city, and an explorer of living spaces. Determined to travel around the world, Philippe unveils how the populations that he encounters claim the space they occupy, shapes it and adjust to it.

programme.title: Yves Saint Laurent
programme.desc: Firestarter. A documentary of a true pioneer of fashion. Sabbatical Entertainment celebrates one of the most influential designers ever as we explore the designer's unparalleled professional acclaim, as well as his fascinating and tumultuous personal life. Yves Saint Laurent can be credited with both spurring the couture's rise in the 1960s as well as the tuxedo suit for women. He was able to adapt his style to accommodate the changes in fashion during his entire career. Sabbatical Entertainment’s... original documentary shows viewers how YSL approached fashion with a different narrative by wanting women to look comfortable yet elegant at the same time.

programme.title: For Our Eyes Only
programme.desc: In “For Our Eyes Only,” get to know all the actors who have embodied the super spy: Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan, and Daniel Craig, their similarities and characteristics that differentiate each one when exhibiting his well-known charm, class and elegance, combined with physical and mental prowess, that makes 007 a real life super hero.

programme.title: Berber: A Quest For Water
programme.desc: In the remote valleys of the Atlas range in Morocco, lies a village Tizi Anoucheg, where water is a rare resource. Berbers are the only people to be found in this harsh environment. They convert the red and dried valleys into a lush green using ancestral irrigation methods. With climate change threatening their very existence one man rises to the occasion & tries to solve the severe water problem.

programme.title: The World's Greatest Carnivals: Quebec Winter Carnival
programme.desc: This 3D documentary special takes us to one of the most colourful and elaborate celebrations on earth where both human creativity and glorious cultures come together. The Quebec Winter Carnival is the world’s largest winter Carnival. It celebrates everything about winter with all sorts of unique competitions and celebrations - from Canoe races across the St. Lawrence River to horse racing with sleds, dog-sledding, skating, ice sculptures, food, music and fun.

programme.title: Volcanic Planet
programme.desc: Volcanoes are the most extreme, dramatic, and explosive forces of nature on our planet. Volcanoes have produced many of the most valuable minerals - and most of the arable soil on earth. Every day, they are exploding around the world. When the Yellowstone Super Volcano blows (and it is now 48,000 years overdue to do so), it will destroy most of life on North America. Award-winning filmmaker Peter Rowe has climbed and filmed 19 volcanoes, and tells the story of them, the adventures of... climbing them, the people who live beside them, and the scientists who risk their lives to study them, in " Volcanic Planet". He also convinces his climbing partner George Kourounis to get married (!?) on the exploding lip of one of them. Filmed in Congo, Iceland, Italy, Vanuatu, Hawaii, Tonga, Turkey, Guatemala, New Zealand, Costa Rica and under the Pacific Ocean, "Volcanic Planet" is a fast-paced high-voltage tour of the world’s most active smoking mountains.

programme.title: The Subversives
programme.desc: Theo van Boven becomes Director of Human Rights for the UN in 1977, where it was impossible to even name a country for gross violations. No bureaucrat, he battles the most repressive regimes of the late 20th century, such as Chile and Argentina and opens the UN door for the first time to "subversive" survivors from across the world. Risking everything, he even takes on the US and the Secretary General.

programme.title: Vacaciones con Fidel
programme.desc: Tristan is a journalist with deep political convictions who worked for years doing journalistic research. Once married and with three children, he accepts a much more remunerative job on commercial television and gradually becomes involved in a life he did not expect.

programme.title: Survivors of the Invisible
programme.desc: One million different species of insects live on Earth. Diving into their world is kind of like adventuring to a faraway and unknown galaxy. With one difference: these living creatures do not live light-years away from us but right under our feet! With unique technologies shots developed by an Austrian entomologist, the film Survivors of the Invisible will make you discover the world of insects as you have never seen it before.

programme.title: Fundamentalism: Is There a Way Back
programme.desc: A growing counter-terrorist movement is gaining worldwide momentum.After the attacks in New York, London, Madrid and Bali as well as the assassinations in Toulouse carried out by Mohamed Merah, the world wonders about how these Islamists came to the point they were able to commit such atrocities: to kill in cold blood and be willing to die a Martyr’s death. How and why did these young men become radicals? Is it reversible?In a number of countries, deradicalization programs have sprung up.... Have they been successful? In this documentary, the first ever of its kind, reporters will meet with s ome Islamists – former terrorists – who have left the path of terror and now dedicate their lives to persuading other terrorists to do the same.

programme.title: Boteti: The Returning River
programme.desc: For 20 years the Boteti River in northern Botswana lay dry, leaving wildlife dependent on a handful of shrinking rain pools. Then, after decades of drought, heavy rains in the Angolan highlands send water flowing once more. Boteti – The Returning River captures this dramatic rebirth, revealing how animals endured the harsh years and how the river’s return transforms the landscape. Filmed over two years in stunning HD, the film documents rare behavior, explosive life, and the renewal of an... entire ecosystem.

programme.title: Against the Tide
programme.desc: Albert (21) decides to fight cancer on his own terms while striving to help others around the world going through the same traumatic experience.

programme.title: Under the Lights: Pelé
programme.desc: (Under the Lights: Pele) A biography of the greatest player of all time on the pitch and one of the most iconic legends in sport.

programme.title: Isetenkheb's Egyptian Coffin
programme.desc: Follow from the amazing restoration process of one of the most cherished and mysterious pieces of History: an Egyptian sarcophagus covered with hieroglyphics (painted wood). With exclusive interviews of experts, art curators and restorators, discover everything about the story of the Isetenkheb coffin of Ancient Egypt dated from around 664-500 BC.

programme.title: Nature's Force
programme.desc: Weather is universal and it's also Extra Terrestrial. Learn about space weather and how it can impact us on earth. Supercells are unique storms that scientists have learnt to measure into three types. Under the earth's crust, nature is extremely energetic, and we see this through the Volcano which acts as our eye into the forces beneath our feet. Learn about the purple buzzing glow called St Elmo's Fire, how it was named and were to look for it.

programme.title: Nature's Force
programme.desc: The beauty, magic, and the science behind the Auroras at both ends of the earth, show them to be more than just a protective magnetic layer. The technology used to measure Wind Speed is finely calibrated with an interesting formula. The Tides remind us of our connection to the moon and our place in the solar system and are monitored for any significant change can have implications for industry, communities, and our ocean life. Earthquakes often make news headlines so how are they measured... and predicted and what can we learn from them about our planet? Acid Rain is a manufactured weather ev ent, the result of manmade industry mixing with nature to result in international treaties to lessen emissions and pollution.

programme.desc: BC Central Coast Salmon Safari Running Southbound outside on Central Coast with a big Tyee Chinook Release finish North of Milbanke Sound.

programme.title: Wild Australia with Ray Mears
programme.desc: In Victoria’s bushland, Ray Mears searches for kangaroos and koalas, then takes a canoe onto a lake to look for the elusive duck-billed platypus.

programme.title: Sarah Shark
programme.desc: Sarah travels to one of the top 10 dive destinations in Australia (Julian Rocks, Byron Bay, NSW) to dive with three species of Wobbegong Sharks within the Cape Byron Marine Park. She also conducts a street poll with members of the public to find out what they think about sharks.

programme.title: Outta Town Adventures
programme.desc: Outta Town Adventures travels both near and far to discover the best advenures the destinations have to offer. Season 1 visits attractions from California to Rwanda, Switzerland, Iceland, Utah, Zambia, Mexico, The Grand Canyon, Georgia (the Eastern European one) Louisiana, Hawaii, Mauritius and Seychelles. This TV series is dedicated to presenting history, culture and geography in a fun and pisitive way. It encourages people to explore this beautiful world - something that starts with simply... getting out of town.

programme.title: Show Me Where You Live
programme.desc: Show me where you live is a documentary series that aims to answer the following question: How can human beings claim ownership to a space so that they can live safely within it, function as a society, and above all be in harmony with the environment around them? As we discover cultures and emblematic populations, we follow Philippe Simay who is at the heart of Inhabiting the World and represents its identity and originality. Philippe takes us on an epic adventure around the Human Habitat... and sets the tone for the journey. As a humanist and philosopher, Philippe is a tireless surveyor of t he city, and an explorer of living spaces. Determined to travel around the world, Philippe unveils how the populations that he encounters claim the space they occupy, shapes it and adjust to it.

programme.desc: From the skyscrapers of Shanghai to the mountainous peaks of "The Last Shangri-La", explore the breathtaking landscape of this incredible country and connect with the people that infuse China's everyday life with flavor, passion and prosperity. Through the eyes of a cultural academic, a laborer, an architect, an urban planner, and a photographer, the grand evolution of a little fishing village is illustrated and documented to reveal one of the fastest growing megacities in the world. And... while the physical landscape gracefully moves towards the future, beliefs, behaviors, and practices are put into test. The changes brought by the Thirty Year Miracle are indeed immense, and it has left no stone, no life, unturned.
